out-of-pocket costs of gathering information concerning the applicant, including, but not limited to, the cost of using a tenant screening service or a consumer credit reporting service, and the reasonable value of time spent by the landlord or their agent in obtaining information on the applicant. In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. out-of-pocket costs of gathering information concerning the applicant, including, but not limited to, the cost of using a tenant screening service or a consumer credit reporting service, and the reasonable value of time spent by the landlord or their agent in obtaining information on the applicant. In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. the twelve month period ending the previous June 30. In determining the allowable
percentage rent increase, numbers of .04 and below shall be rounded down to the nearest

tenth decimal place. In no event, however, shall the allowable annual adjustment be less

Any payment or deposit of monies by the tenant, the primary function of which is to secure
the performance of a rental agreement or any part of such agreement, including an
advance payment of rent, shall be held by the landlord, in a fiduciary capacity for the
benefit of the tenant and shall accrue simple interest at the rate equal to the average rates
of interest paid on six-month certificates of deposit by banks doing business in the City
until such time as the payment or deposit is returned to the tenant or entitled to be used
by the landlord as provided in Civil Code Section 1950.5. The interest accrued by said
payment or deposit through October 31st of each year shall be returned to the tenant
annually in December of each year, either through a rent rebate or cash payment, and
shall be at a rate equal to the 12-month average of the average rates of interest paid on
six-month certificates of deposit by banks doing business in the City on the first business

nearest tenth. On or before November 15th of each year, the Board shall give public
notice of the rate to be effective for the following December.

Any payment or deposit of monies by the tenant, the primary function of which is to secure
the performance of a rental agreement or any part of such agreement, including an
advance payment of rent, shall be held by the landlord, in a fiduciary capacity for the
benefit of the tenant and shall accrue simple interest at the rate equal to the average rates
of interest paid on six-month certificates of deposit by banks doing business in the City
until such time as the payment or deposit is returned to the tenant or entitled to be used
by the landlord as provided in Civil Code Section 1950.5. The interest accrued by said
payment or deposit through October 31st of each year shall be returned to the tenant
annually in December of each year, either through a rent rebate or cash payment, and
shall be at a rate equal to the 12-month average of the average rates of interest paid on
six-month certificates of deposit by banks doing business in the City on the first business
day of each month for the prior 12 months ending on November 1st, rounded to the
nearest tenth. On or before November 15th of each year, the Board shall give public
notice of the rate to be effective for the following December.

notice of the rate to be effective for the following December.

Any payment or deposit of monies by the tenant, the primary function of which is to secure
the performance of a rental agreement or any part of such agreement, including an
advance payment of rent, shall be held by the landlord, in a fiduciary capacity for the
benefit of the tenant and shall accrue simple interest at the rate equal to the average rates
of interest paid on six-month certificates of deposit by banks doing business in the City
until such time as the payment or deposit is returned to the tenant or entitled to be used
by the landlord as provided in Civil Code Section 1950.5. The interest accrued by said
payment or deposit through October 31st of each year shall be returned to the tenant
annually in December of each year, either through a rent rebate or cash payment, and
shall be at a rate equal to the 12-month average of the average rates of interest paid on
six-month certificates of deposit by banks doing business in the City on the first business
day of each month for the prior 12 months ending on November 1st, rounded to the
nearest tenth. On or before November 15th of each year, the Board shall give public
notice of the rate to be effective for the following December.
results.plain_language: Landlords must hold security deposits in a fiduciary capacity and pay tenants annual simple interest on the deposit every December (or upon move-out), calculated using the 12-month average of interest rates paid on six-month CDs by local banks.

An owner or lessee may not require more than a sum equal to 1 1/2 times 1 month's rental
according to the terms of contract, lease, or agreement as a security for the use or rental of real
property used for dwelling purposes. Whenever an owner or lessee collects from a tenant an
additional amount of security deposit, the amount collected annually as additional security shall
not be greater than 10 percent of the current security deposit.
results.plain_language: An owner or lessee may not require more than 1 1/2 times 1 month's rental as security deposit for real property used for dwelling purposes, and any additional security deposit collected annually shall not exceed 10 percent of the current security deposit.
results.plain_language_es: Un propietario o arrendatario no puede exigir más de 1 1/2 veces el alquiler de 1 mes como depósito de seguridad para bienes inmuebles destinados a vivienda, y cualquier depósito de seguridad adicional cobrado anualmente no debe exceder el 10 por ciento del depósito de seguridad actual.

results.reason: coverage depends on facts not in the data: owner_occupied, units
results.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding
an applicant's criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer, except that a housing provider may consider whether
an applicant has ever been convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine
on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under
a State sex offender registration program.
(2) A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant's criminal record prior to making a
conditional offer.
results.plain_language: Landlords cannot inquire into an applicant's criminal history before making a conditional offer, except for specific lifetime sex offender registration or methamphetamine manufacturing convictions. Even after a conditional offer, only certain serious or recent convictions may be considered, and the landlord must perform an individualized assessment and provide specific written disclosures before withdrawing an offer.
results.plain_language_es: Los propietarios no pueden consultar el historial penal de un solicitante antes de hacer una oferta condicional, salvo en casos específicos de registro de por vida para delincuentes sexuales o condenas por fabricación de metanfetamina. Incluso después de una oferta condicional, solo se pueden considerar ciertas condenas graves o recientes, y el arrendador debe realizar una evaluación individualizada y proporcionar notificaciones específicas por escrito antes de retirar una oferta.

results.quoted_span:
No lessee or tenant or the assigns, under-tenants or legal representatives of such lessee or tenant may be
removed by the Superior Court from any house, building, mobile home or land in a mobile home park or
tenement leased for residential purposes, other than (1) owner-occupied premises with not more than two
rental units or a hotel, motel or other guest house or part thereof rented to a transient guest or seasonal
tenant; (2) a dwelling unit which is held in trust on behalf of a member of the immediate family of the person
or persons establishing the trust, provided that the member of the immediate family on whose behalf the
trust is established permanently occupies the unit; and (3) a dwelling unit which is permanently occupied by
a member of the immediate family of the owner of that unit, provided, however, that exception (2) or (3)
shall apply only in cases in which the member of the immediate family has a developmental disability,
except upon establishment of one of the following grounds as good cause:
results.plain_language: Landlords cannot evict residential tenants or refuse lease renewals except upon establishing one of the enumerated statutory grounds for good cause.
results.plain_language_es: Los propietarios no pueden desalojar a inquilinos residenciales ni negarse a renovar el contrato de arrendamiento excepto si demuestran una de las causas justificadas enumeradas en la ley.

The amount of the application screening fee shall not be greater than the actual
out-of-pocket costs of gathering information concerning the applicant, including, but not limited to, the cost of using a tenant screening service or a consumer credit reporting service, and the reasonable value of time spent by the landlord or their agent in obtaining information on the applicant. In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. results.plain_language_es: El propietario no puede desalojar a un inquilino sin una causa justificada contemplada en uno de los diez motivos enumerados. Para desalojos por mudanza del propietario o un familiar, se requiere asistencia estándar de reubicación de $15,000 (más $5,000 para personas de bajos ingresos, discapacitadas, de la tercera edad, menores o contratos anteriores a 1999).

results.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
results.plain_language: Landlords cannot terminate a tenancy without stating an allowed at-fault or no-fault just cause once all tenants have continuously occupied the unit for at least 12 months (or 24 months if adult tenants were added). For no-fault evictions, the landlord must provide relocation assistance equal to one month of rent or waive the final month's rent.
results.plain_language_es: Los propietarios no pueden rescindir un contrato de arrendamiento sin declarar una causa justa permitida (con o sin culpa) una vez que todos los inquilinos hayan ocupado continuamente la vivienda durante al menos 12 meses (o 24 meses si se añadieron adultos). En los desalojos sin culpa, el propietario debe proporcionar asistencia para la reubicación equivalente a un mes de alquiler o condonar el alquiler del último mes.

results.quoted_span:
Any payment or deposit of monies by the tenant, the primary function of which is to secure
the performance of a rental agreement or any part of such agreement, including an
advance payment of rent, shall be held by the landlord, in a fiduciary capacity for the
benefit of the tenant and shall accrue simple interest at the rate equal to the average rates
of interest paid on six-month certificates of deposit by banks doing business in the City
until such time as the payment or deposit is returned to the tenant or entitled to be used
by the landlord as provided in Civil Code Section 1950.5. The interest accrued by said
payment or deposit through October 31st of each year shall be returned to the tenant
annually in December of each year, either through a rent rebate or cash payment, and
shall be at a rate equal to the 12-month average of the average rates of interest paid on
six-month certificates of deposit by banks doing business in the City on the first business
day of each month for the prior 12 months ending on November 1st, rounded to the
nearest tenth. On or before November 15th of each year, the Board shall give public
notice of the rate to be effective for the following December.
results.plain_language: Landlords must hold security deposits in a fiduciary capacity and pay tenants annual simple interest on the deposit every December (or upon move-out), calculated using the 12-month average of interest rates paid on six-month CDs by local banks.
results.plain_language_es: Los propietarios deben mantener los depósitos de seguridad en calidad fiduciaria y pagar a los inquilinos un interés simple anual sobre el depósito cada diciembre (o al desocupar la vivienda), calculado con el promedio de 12 meses de las tasas de interés pagadas en certificados de depósito (CD) a seis meses por bancos locales.

results.quoted_span:
The amount of the application screening fee shall not be greater than the actual
out-of-pocket costs of gathering information concerning the applicant, including, but not limited to, the cost of using a tenant screening service or a consumer credit reporting service, and the reasonable value of time spent by the landlord or their agent in obtaining information on the applicant. In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
results.plain_language: Landlords may charge an application screening fee capped at actual out-of-pocket costs and no more than $30 (adjusted annually for CPI since 1998). Landlords cannot charge a fee if no unit is available, must provide an itemized receipt, must follow specific first-come or full-refund screening processes, and must refund unused amounts.
results.plain_language_es: Los propietarios pueden cobrar una tarifa de evaluación de solicitud limitada a los costos directos reales y no más de $30 (ajustada anualmente por el IPC desde 1998). No pueden cobrar una tarifa si no hay unidades disponibles, deben proporcionar un recibo desglosado, seguir procesos específicos de selección por orden de llegada o de reembolso total, y devolver los montos no utilizados.

Any payment or deposit of monies by the tenant, the primary function of which is to secure
the performance of a rental agreement or any part of such agreement, including an
advance payment of rent, shall be held by the landlord, in a fiduciary capacity for the
benefit of the tenant and shall accrue simple interest at the rate equal to the average rates
of interest paid on six-month certificates of deposit by banks doing business in the City
until such time as the payment or deposit is returned to the tenant or entitled to be used
by the landlord as provided in Civil Code Section 1950.5. The interest accrued by said
payment or deposit through October 31st of each year shall be returned to the tenant
annually in December of each year, either through a rent rebate or cash payment, and
shall be at a rate equal to the 12-month average of the average rates of interest paid on
six-month certificates of deposit by banks doing business in the City on the first business
day of each month for the prior 12 months ending on November 1st, rounded to the
nearest tenth. On or before November 15th of each year, the Board shall give public
notice of the rate to be effective for the following December.

out-of-pocket costs of gathering information concerning the applicant, including, but not limited to, the cost of using a tenant screening service or a consumer credit reporting service, and the reasonable value of time spent by the landlord or their agent in obtaining information on the applicant.
